look_here_first: Ignore ray color first. Look for very narrow rough leaves and a usually single head on a stout little-branched stem, with drooping rays around a hard prickly cone.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: deep-rooted perennial from stout taproot/crown; narrow linear-lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate rough/hairy leaves; stems stout and usually simple or weakly branched, often one head; ray florets often droop around a broad hard prickly conical disk; pappus much reduced compared with fluffy Asteraceae

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Deep-rooted perennial, usually not a spreading rhizomatous colony.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Radiate head with pink-purple rays around strongly conical prickly disk.

key_traits.label: Reproductive detail
key_traits.text: Stiff chaff/bracts among disk florets create the prickly cone.

lookalikes.differences: Ratibida has an elongated columnar disk and deeply divided leaves. E. purpurea generally has much broader leaves; E. pallida overlap requires finer floral/leaf characters and range context.
